title: Deadlock in Multi-Pool Resource Checkout (Order Inversion)
pattern: Different threads or functions attempting to checkout resources from multiple distinct pools (such as a database connection pool and a messaging/master-repo connection pool) in different relative order.
why_bad: If Thread A calls `run_create_transaction` and acquires DB connection, while Thread B calls `run_update_transaction` and acquires Master Repo connection, they block each other [151]. Under high load, DB pool connections are depleted by `create` threads and Repo connections are depleted by `update` threads [151]. This results in a deadlocked state where no thread can progress, hanging the system indefinitely [151].
detection: Identify functions that acquire locks or checkout resources from multiple pools/mutexes concurrently, and verify if the order of acquisition is inconsistent across different paths.
fix: Enforce a strict, uniform ordering constraint for acquiring resources across all execution pathways in the codebase [151].
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code*, Chapter 16 / passage [151]; Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!*, Chapter 10 / passage [231].
